title: SRVUSD 5th Grade Placement Prep — 6-Week Calendar
subtitle: Stories + Famous Mathematicians + Practice Problems
goal: Master fluency, problem translation, and multi-step reasoning for Course 1/2/3 placement

weeks.title: Foundation: Multi-Digit Fluency & Word Problems
weeks.focus: Building speed with multiplication/division; translating English to math

relatedStories.title: The Chessboard & Rice (exponential growth)
relatedStories.reason: Shows why multiplication is powerful; introduces doubling/exponential concepts

relatedStories.title: Penny Doubling
relatedStories.reason: Real money scenario; makes multiplication meaningful

relatedMathematicians.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Found a shortcut to add 1+2+3+...+100 in seconds
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Shows how pattern-finding beats brute-force calculation

practiceTopics: Word problem: Reading → Setting up the math
sampleProblems: A school has 245 students. Each classroom holds 28 students. How many classrooms are needed?

weeks.title: Decimals & Fractions (Addition/Subtraction)
weeks.focus: Operating with fractional parts of wholes; converting between forms

relatedStories.title: The Invention of Zero
relatedStories.reason: Shows how humans invented NOTHING as a number; fractions didn't make sense without 0

relatedMathematicians.name: Ancient Indian Mathematicians
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Invented zero and decimal system (~500 CE)
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Without zero, fractions and decimals are impossible

sampleProblems: A recipe uses 2.5 cups of flour per batch. How much flour is needed for 4 batches?

weeks.title: Ratios & Unit Rates (High Priority)

relatedStories.title: What is a Ratio?
relatedStories.reason: Apples to oranges, cats to dogs; everyday ratio scenarios

relatedStories.title: Unit Rates
relatedStories.reason: Cost per muffin, miles per hour; real shopping/travel applications

relatedStories.title: Soccer Penalty Kick Probability
relatedStories.reason: Ratios show success rates; why practice matters

relatedMathematicians.name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Saw number patterns instantly; understood ratios & fractions deeply
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Ratios are hidden everywhere in math

practiceTopics: Unit rates (cost per item, speed per hour)
sampleProblems: If 3 notebooks cost $6, what is the unit rate?
A map scale is 1 inch = 5 miles. How many miles is 7 inches?
A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. What is the speed per hour?

weeks.title: Expressions & Equations (High Priority)
weeks.focus: Writing math from English; solving for unknown

relatedMathematicians.name: René Descartes
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Invented the coordinate system so flies on ceilings can be described mathematically
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Variables (x, y) let us describe ANY position, ANY unknown

practiceTopics: Evaluating expressions with variables (3x + 5 when x = 7)
Writing expressions from words ('5 more than twice a number')
sampleProblems: Write an expression: 'The cost of 3 items at $4.50 each, minus a $5 coupon'

weeks.title: Geometry & Spatial Reasoning
weeks.focus: Area, volume, coordinate plane; connecting to real buildings/objects

relatedStories.title: Egyptian Right Triangle (3-4-5)
relatedStories.reason: Ancient builders used this to make perfect corners; shows geometry's history

relatedStories.title: Honeycomb Hexagons
relatedStories.reason: Nature's geometry; why bees are brilliant mathematicians

relatedMathematicians.name: Euclid
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Organized all geometry into logical rules (Elements, 300 BCE)
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Area & volume formulas come from geometric logic

practiceTopics: Area of rectangles & triangles (base × height formulas)
Perimeter of rectangles (and solving for missing sides)
Volume of rectangular prisms (length × width × height)
sampleProblems: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 and height 6.
Find the volume of a prism with dimensions 4 × 3 × 5.
A rectangle has perimeter 50. Length is 15. Find width.
A rectangle is 12 by 8. What is its area?

weeks.title: Statistics, Probability & Mixed Review
weeks.focus: Data interpretation; chance; integrating all 5 weeks

relatedStories.title: Birthday Paradox
relatedStories.reason: Surprising probability result; why intuition fails in statistics

relatedStories.title: Tic-Tac-Toe Strategy
relatedStories.reason: Counting outcomes; why games are mathematical

relatedMathematicians.name: Florence Nightingale
relatedMathematicians.achievement: Used data visualization (rose diagrams) to save lives during the Crimean War
relatedMathematicians.lesssonConnection: Statistics & graphs tell stories that numbers alone cannot

practiceTopics: Interpreting bar graphs, line plots, data displays
Multi-step word problems mixing all domains
sampleProblems: A bag has 3 red, 2 blue, 5 green marbles. What is P(red)?
A student scores 85, 90, 95 on three tests. What score is needed on the 4th test to average 90?
A shirt costs $24 with a 25% discount. What is the final price?

course1.title: Course 1 (Traditional 6th Grade)
course1.description: Solid 5th grade foundation; ready for core 6th grade curriculum at standard pace

course2.title: Course 2 (Accelerated 6th Grade)
course2.description: Strong grasp of ratios, algebra, geometry; ready for faster pace and challenge

course3.title: Course 3 (Advanced; Algebra Focus)
course3.description: Mastery of concepts AND speed; ready for algebra-heavy curriculum with proofs/extensions
